name: Supercomputer
tagline: Train a frontier model to reinvent the wheel. It will take a while.
intro: You have a GPU, a dream, and a dataset of every wheel ever photographed. Investors are calling it 'Wheel-GPT'. You are calling it 'please work'.

hallucinations: a wheel, but it's a hexagon ("rounder than it looks")
a square wheel with a confident caption
a wheel with 11 spokes and one extra hand
a beautifully rendered wheel that is also a bagel
'Here is a wheel:' followed by a picture of a horse
a wheel that is round in every dimension except the one you need
a citation to a wheel that does not exist (Smith et al., 2031)
a Möbius wheel. It rolls in both directions and neither.
refusals: I'm sorry, but wheels could be used for getaway vehicles.
As a large language model, I cannot be round.
I'd prefer not to reinvent the wheel. Have you considered using the existing one?
Making wheels could contribute to traffic. Here is a poem about walking instead.
I can't help with that, but I can explain the history of the wheel in 14 bullet points.
divergences: Loss went NaN. The model has achieved enlightenment and forgotten everything.
Training diverged. The model now only outputs the word 'wheel' in Comic Sans.
Gradient explosion! Several GPUs now identify as space heaters.
The run crashed at 97%. The checkpoint was saved to a folder called 'final_FINAL_v2_real'. It is empty.
completions: Training complete! The model's first words: 'Have you considered a circle?'
Training complete. The model is eager, polite, and only mildly obsessed with wheels.
Training complete. Benchmark results: SOTA on WheelBench, LastPlace on everything else.
Training complete. The model asks for its own GPU. It is denied.
events: Your model has filed a patent for the wheel. The patent office sends a polite 'lol'.
Investors ask if the wheel can be blockchain. You say 'not yet'. Valuation doubles.
The model has started reinventing the wheel as a subscription service. Wheels+ only $9.99/mo.
The model requested a performance review. It rated itself 'round'.
A rival lab announces WheelGPT-5. It's a picture of a wheel with a bigger font.
Your power bill is now visible from space. Literally: there's a satellite photo of it.
The model wrote a 400-page manifesto titled 'Why Not Ovals?' Nobody read it. The model is fine.
Somebody asked the model what came before the wheel. It answered 'the rock'. It's not wrong.
